answer: Colocation attestation binds each identity to a unique physical power draw measured at the outlet. A validator samples the opal-tinged current signature per agent and rejects any second identity sharing the same meter. Because one operator cannot run two CPUs off one metered socket without detectable overlap, each fake identity needs its own power feed, costing roughly a full node's electricity plus hardware per sybil. The residual plume of switching noise flags cloned hardware, and the yarrow-like spikiness of shared rails makes masking expensive.
